newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes up on dollar sales.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes up on dollar sales.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee came off the day's low to close up against the dollar on Thursday, due to late selling of the greenback by a state bank, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.57 to the dollar, after opening at 58.60 and falling to a low of 58.67, they said.
"The rupee recovered when a state bank sold dollars after it (dollar) rose to 58.67 rupees," said a local bank dealer.
The dollar rose early on import covering and some speculative buying of the grenback, which was encouraged by low call money rates, dealers said.
"With call money at the bottom at nine percent, some banks are moving into dollars," said a Hatton National Bank dealer.
The Central Bank's overnight repo rate is at 8.75 percent.
